candidate: Claude Code `/doctor prompt-audit` (documented at Claude Code v2.1.322)

candidate: Analyst and reviewer read files with the agent's own bounded read and search tools, not POSIX shell tools
what: Replace `tail -n 200`, `grep -n -m 50`, `sed -n`, `head -n` and `sha256sum` in both agent bodies with instructions to read line ranges and to search with a result limit.
problem_here: The named commands do not exist in PowerShell on native Windows, and other agents' shells differ.
mechanism: Wording in both agent bodies; the shell stays only for `expctl` and read-only `git`.
evidence: Kit files read 2026-11-11 (`run-analyst.md` line 23, `experiment-reviewer.md` lines 20 to 22; `expctl.py` has no log-reading subcommand); https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/best-practices (do not assume tools are installed).
maturity: Uses tools every target agent has.
cost: The bound is set by instruction, not by code.
simpler_alternative: none smaller; the heavier option is a new bounded log subcommand in `expctl`.
reason: Smallest change that makes both agent files work on Windows and in other agents.
cheap_local_trial: On native Windows ask the analyst one question about a saved log and check that it uses no POSIX-only command.

candidate: Fresh agent session per loop iteration, with state carried in files
what: Each unattended iteration starts a new session whose first prompt is fixed and whose context comes from the journal, `expctl status` and run artifacts.
problem_here: Long single sessions accumulate caution and stale notes, depend on compaction, and cannot take instruction changes mid-conversation on the newest model.
mechanism: The loop runner starts the agent CLI non-interactively per iteration; the worker prompt and settings never change inside a session; waiting on long runs is done by the harness.
evidence: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices (multi-window work: state files, progress notes, git; a fresh window reads them), https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompting-claude-fable-5-2 (caution builds up; instruction changes belong in new conversations), https://code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog (a v2.1.321 fix note says non-interactive sessions stop background commands after 10 minutes; read through a summary); checked 2026-11-11.
maturity: Vendor-recommended pattern; the kit already keeps its state in files.
cost: Start-up tokens per iteration; each iteration must rebuild context from files.
simpler_alternative: One long session with compaction.
reason: Matches vendor guidance and the kit's file-based state, and keeps the prompt prefix stable.
cheap_local_trial: Run two back-to-back non-interactive iterations on a toy repo and check that the second picks up the first one's journal entry without any shared conversation.

candidate: Read-only rule for the reviewer and the analyst enforced in the settings-level guard, keyed on agent type

problem_here: The subagents' read-only guarantee rests on a hook declared in each agent file. Claude Code skips a project subagent's own hooks in a folder nobody trusted, which includes a `-p` run, and on native Windows that hook's `python3` command probably cannot start (row 21). An unattended run in a fresh clone therefore has no read-only layer in either subagent.
mechanism: Hooks from settings files also run inside subagents, and their input carries `agent_id` and `agent_type`. `nn_guard.py` already reads `agent_type` for its log, its command is rewritten to the chosen interpreter by the installer, and it has `onFailure: block`; add one branch that calls the existing checks of `nn_readonly.py` for those two agent types.
evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks and https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents, read through page summaries on 2026-11-11 and cross-checked with the quotes in the platform note in this folder (`platform-claude-code.md`), whose candidate row 14 is the same proposal; kit files `.claude/hooks/nn_guard.py` (line 425), `.claude/hooks/nn_readonly.py` and `settings.fragment.json` (lines 54 to 62) read 2026-11-11. Not run.
maturity: Documented hook input fields; both pieces of code already exist in the kit.
cost: A few lines in the guard plus tests; the two agent names become part of the guard's contract; Claude Code only, so the Cursor and Codex ports still need their own read-only route (rows 22, 24 and 25).
simpler_alternative: Keep the frontmatter hook and document that the folder must be trusted before an unattended run.
reason: Moves the guarantee to the settings-level hook, which per the vendor pages quoted in the platform note also runs in an untrusted non-interactive session, and which the installer already makes start on Windows.
cheap_local_trial: In a scratch install start a non-interactive session in a folder that was never trusted, have the reviewer attempt a shell write, and look in the guard log for a denial that names the agent type.

candidate: Block file-tool writes outside the working directories in unattended sessions (`permissions.blockWritesOutsideWorkingDirectories`, Claude Code v2.1.314)
what: A setting that refuses Write, Edit and NotebookEdit calls on paths outside the session's working directories.
problem_here: An unattended loop worker should not edit files outside the project. The kit's guard denies sealed test data and edits inside an active run's folder, and its header lists no rule about paths outside the project.
mechanism: The key can be set in any settings file, so the kit's project settings or the loop's `--settings` file can carry it; a repository can turn the block on for itself but cannot lift a user's; exceptions come only from `/add-dir`, `--add-dir` or `additionalDirectories` in user or managed settings; the worktree tools are removed or refused while it is on.
evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference and https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions, read through page summaries with quoted entries on 2026-11-11 (scope any settings file; it does not limit shell commands, MCP tools or the programs hooks run); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog (v2.1.314); kit file `.claude/hooks/nn_guard.py` lines 1 to 27 read 2026-11-11. No behaviour test.
maturity: Documented setting added in v2.1.314; untested here.
cost: Covers the file tools only, so shell writes still need the guard; it switches off worktree use, which a design with one worktree per experiment would need; Claude Code only.
simpler_alternative: A path check in the kit's own guard hook, which also sees shell arguments.
reason: One documented line that narrows the loop worker's reach, but it is untested here, covers file tools only and conflicts with worktree-based designs.
cheap_local_trial: In an updated Claude Code set the key in a scratch project's settings and ask the agent to write a file in the parent folder, first with the Write tool and then with a shell redirect; the first should be refused, and the second shows what the guard must still cover.

candidate: Claude Code auto memory as the store for run state and lessons
what: Let the agent's built-in memory notes carry which runs are live, what was approved and what was learned from one session to the next.
problem_here: State must survive context summaries and new sessions. The kit already keeps it in the journal and in `expctl status`.
mechanism: Claude Code writes notes to a memory folder on the machine and loads the first 200 lines or 25 KB at session start and again after compaction.
evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory (load limits, re-injection after compaction, stored per machine), https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents (subagents do not load the main conversation's auto memory; read through a page summary), https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompting-claude-fable-5-2 (stale cautions in notes and memories accumulate and should be deleted); checked 2026-11-11.
maturity: Documented feature of one agent.
cost: State outside the repository that the reviewer, the analyst, other agents and other machines cannot see; not versioned with the experiments; the model decides what is written and nothing prunes it.
simpler_alternative: The append-only journal plus `expctl status`, which the kit already has.
reason: The journal already holds this state in a file that every agent, subagent and machine can read and that a reviewer can audit.
cheap_local_trial: none

candidate: Self-paced `/loop` as the wait mechanism for long runs (the skill's current advice)
what: The agent schedules its own next wake-up while a training run is in progress instead of holding a shell command open.
problem_here: SKILL.md recommends `/loop` and a scheduled wake-up for long waits. Since v2.1.319 a self-paced loop ends when a turn finishes without rescheduling, and the mechanism does not survive a resumed session.
mechanism: Self-paced `/loop` picks a delay between one minute and one hour; an iteration that neither reschedules nor stops gets one fallback wake-up about 20 minutes later, and the loop ends if that one does not reschedule either; tasks fire only while Claude Code is running and idle; a self-paced loop is not restored by `--resume`, background commands are not restarted on resume, and recurring tasks expire after 7 days.
evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks, read as raw text on 2026-11-11, and https://code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog (v2.1.319, 2026-11-06; read through a page summary); kit file `.claude/skills/nn-training/SKILL.md` lines 23 and 42 to 47 read 2026-11-11. No behaviour test.
maturity: Documented feature whose end conditions changed five days before the check.
cost: A loop that ends without notice leaves a run unwatched; Claude Code only and interactive only; each wake-up resends the session context (open question 8 in the note).
simpler_alternative: Wait on `expctl watch` as a background or monitored command, which the skill also describes; in the unattended loop the harness does the waiting (row 47).
reason: It is in the core skill today and its end conditions changed this month; keep it only as the interactive fallback if a re-test shows that a missed reschedule is noticed, and never as the unattended loop's wait.
cheap_local_trial: In an updated Claude Code start a 30-minute toy run, wait with a self-paced `/loop`, let one iteration end without rescheduling and see whether the agent still reports the end of the run; then resume the session and check again.

candidate: Cost-first delegation wording, kept in each agent's own file
what: Replace standing `use the subagent` lines with wording that states the cost first, says when delegation is and is not worth it and how to brief, and keep that wording per agent.
problem_here: The block, SKILL.md and its gates carry standing delegation lines. On the newest Claude model such lines raise cost, while the newest OpenAI model delegates less than wanted, so one shared sentence over-triggers one agent and under-triggers the other.
mechanism: Edits B6 and S6 in the note: the reviewer gate stays, with the cases where it is not needed (smoke runs, reverted changes); the analyst line becomes a size rule; delegation text for each agent lives in that agent's mechanics reference (row 20).
evidence: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompting-claude-fable-5-2 and https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/fable-5-2/whats-new-fable-5-2 (subagents can be a large share of session cost; cost-first wording gave about a third less delegation at equal task success), https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices (delegation does not improve an answer; the context window is rarely the limit now), https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-guidance (the model delegates less than wanted; read through a summary); checked 2026-11-11; vendor-measured, not replicated.
maturity: Vendor guidance for the current models.
cost: Wording only; less delegation puts more raw log into the main context, so the size rule needs a number; untested on any model.
simpler_alternative: Delete the standing delegation lines and leave delegation to each model's default.
reason: Vendor-measured cost reduction at equal success, and the only wording approach that serves two agents whose defaults pull in opposite directions.
cheap_local_trial: Run one toy campaign with the old and the new block and count subagent calls and total tokens.

candidate: Research scout on the latest Opus or Fable model at `high`, never `low`
what: Model and effort setting for the optional, network-using research scout: Opus 5.5 or Fable 5.2 at `high`.
problem_here: The upgrade adds an optional research scout. At `low` effort a model searches less and answers from memory, which defeats a scout whose job is to check what changed.
mechanism: `model` and `effort` keys in the optional module's config or in the scout's agent file; no model name in shared prompts.
evidence: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompting-claude-fable-5-2 (`high` for research and long unattended work), https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompting-claude-fable-5-1 (at `low` the model searches less), https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/effort (per-model starting levels), https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/refusals-and-fallback (machine-learning content can be refused and billed); checked 2026-11-11. No measurement for this kit.
maturity: Vendor guidance for the current models.
cost: The highest cost per call of the kit's roles (4/20 or 8/40 USD per million tokens, plus search results in context); fetched pages are an injection path; a refusal on machine-learning content can end a scout run.
simpler_alternative: No scout: the user supplies sources, or the main agent searches when asked.
reason: If the optional scout exists, `high` is the documented setting for research and `low` is documented to search less; the module stays opt-in because it needs network.
cheap_local_trial: Ask the scout one question whose answer changed after the model's training cutoff, at `low` and at `high`, and compare whether it searched and what it cited.

candidate: Lower automatic compaction threshold to cut cost in long sessions
what: Set a smaller compaction window so that a long session is summarised earlier.
problem_here: A long campaign on a 1M-token window resends a large context at every wake-up (open question 8 in the note).
mechanism: `/autocompact`, the `autoCompactWindow` setting or `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW`, each accepting 100,000 to 1,000,000 tokens; the default on 1M-window models is about 967,000.
evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config and https://code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog (setting, range and default), https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices and https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompting-claude-fable-5-1 (aggressive context management is old advice; compacting early to save cost can cost intelligence), https://code.claude.com/docs/en/context-window (what survives a compaction); checked 2026-11-11. No cost measurement.
maturity: Documented setting.
cost: Each compaction drops the skill body beyond its first 5,000 tokens and the context that hooks added earlier, and can lose approvals and rejected ideas that exist only in the conversation; Claude Code only.
simpler_alternative: A fresh session per loop iteration with state in files (row 47), and `/clear` between unrelated tasks.
reason: The vendor advises against compacting early for cost, the saving is unmeasured, and the kit's state already lives in files.
cheap_local_trial: Measure tokens per wake-up in one long toy session at the default window and at 200,000.

candidate: Per-step harness reminders (budget countdown, status line or repeated rule after every tool result)
what: Hook or harness text added to the conversation after every tool result, such as remaining budget, a status line or a rule repeated on each step.
problem_here: A loop design may want to keep the remaining budget and the rules in front of the worker at every step. Today the kit's settings add context only at session start and after compaction, and the guard speaks only when it denies or asks.
mechanism: A PostToolUse hook or a harness wrapper that injects text on every step.
evidence: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompting-claude-sonnet-5-5, read as raw text on 2026-11-11 (frequent harness text after tool results, such as a token countdown after every tool result or instructions or context added on every step, can be treated as a possible prompt injection; an occasional one-turn reminder is misread far less often); https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompting-claude-fable-5-2 (removing a large prompt-written budget lowered cost at equal performance); kit file `settings.fragment.json` read 2026-11-11 (hook events SessionStart and PreToolUse only).
maturity: Vendor-documented failure on one current model; not tested on the others.
cost: Tokens on every step, and a worker that starts to distrust harness text may also discount the messages that matter.
simpler_alternative: Budget enforced in harness code, state shown once at session start and after compaction (row 18), and one reminder at a real event such as a budget threshold.
reason: Budgets and limits belong in harness code; per-step text costs tokens and is documented to be misread as an injection attempt.
cheap_local_trial: none
